pages.text: Bung grabbed white rice cake with muddy hands. Brown prints marked it. Little Ddori watched. "Fine! I will eat quickly and carry more!"
Bung was carrying vegetables where the water had gone out. "After I move all these, I will share rice cake with Grandpa!" His rowing boat stood tied to a post.
Soon Bung's tummy gurgled and ached. No lifting the vegetable basket now! "My tummy hurts..." Ddori laid a hand on it.
Grandpa put down his oar and came over. He held the half-eaten cake before Bung's eyes. Three brown handprints on white rice cake!
"This moved from your hands onto the cake." He opened Bung's palm. Black mud filled every crease. "All that was on my hands?"
Grandpa scooped water from the bucket. "Clean hands—yum! One, splash of water!" Bung held both hands under the stream. Mud loosened.
"Two, scrub palms! Three, between the fingers!" Bung drew Ddori's hands close to rub together. Brown water ran off. "Clean hands—yum!"
Clean, squeaky hands! After a short seated rest, the tummy ache settled too. Bung picked up fresh rice cake. No marks this time.
Next day, Bung stopped before the cake basket. "Wait! Water splash, scrub palms, between fingers!" Before Grandpa called, Bung took a scoop.
Grandpa stroked Bung's back with a big hand. Clean hands at meals meant no tummy ache. Bung broke off half the white cake for Ddori. "Clean hands—yum!"
